front: What are the main benefits of converting data to an Excel Table (Ctrl+T)?
back: Formulas and charts that refer to it expand automatically as rows are added, and structured references such as `=SUM(Sales[Amount])` are easier to read than cell ranges.

front: Trap: you change the source data of a PivotTable. Why do the totals not change?
back: PivotTables do not recalculate automatically. You must Refresh (Data > Refresh All), and if new rows fall outside the source range, update the range or base it on a Table.

front: What does a two-variable Data Table do?
back: It recalculates one output formula for every combination of two inputs, using a row input cell and a column input cell. The input cells must be on the same sheet as the table.

front: How does Goal Seek differ from Solver?
back: Goal Seek changes a single input cell until one formula hits a target value. Solver can change many cells and optimize an objective subject to constraints.

front: Which built-in tools help audit a formula's logic?
back: Trace Precedents and Trace Dependents draw arrows between linked cells, Evaluate Formula steps through a calculation, and Ctrl+` toggles showing formulas instead of values.
